title: Pricebook Consolidation & Discount Exception Policy
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: multiple ad-hoc pricebook entries and informal discount practices have led to inconsistent pricing, audit exposure for enterprise deals, and oversized discounts without proper security/compliance gating. Goal: consolidate the canonical pricebook, codify a discount exception policy with clear thresholds and role-based approvals, and wire the approval path into CPQ/Salesforce + internal audit so that enterprise security questionnaires trigger additional review steps.
acceptance_criteria:
- Canonical pricebook V1 published and deployed to internal admin UI and CPQ.
- Discount exception thresholds and approvers documented and visible in Salesforce quote UI.
- Automated approval flow created for 15-30% discounts (RevOps), and manual review path for >30% with legal/security hooks.
- Audit trail created: every exception must include reason, originating AE, approvals, and associated SQ (security questionnaire) link.
- Migration plan for existing active quotes (>USD 50k) with inconsistent discounts executed or flagged.
decisions: Adopt unified token/embedding/dedicated SKU structure in canonical pricebook to simplify bundling and discount math.
Set auto-approval threshold for AEs up to 15% for self-serve and SMB motions.
Require RevOps approval for 15-30% discount ranges with automated Slack + email notification and RevOps one-click approve/deny in Salesforce.
Mandate CRO + Legal + Security review for discounts >30% or deals with security questionnaire flagged as high-risk.
Implement 90-day time-to-live on all discount exceptions; renewals require re-approval if above baseline.
Pricebook changes behind feature-flag for gradual rollout and metric observation (feature flag: pricebook_v1_consolidation).

next_steps: Run canary on 5 active AE accounts with feature-flag enabled, monitor approval latency and deal conversion impact for 2 weeks.
notes: Trade-offs considered: tight discount caps reduce ACV loss but can slow closing velocity on strategic deals. We prioritized automated low-touch approvals for common cases (<=15%) to protect velocity while routing higher-risk discounts through RevOps + security. Implementation choices: prefer minimal CPQ schema changes and keep heavy validation logic in RevOps microservice to enable iterative changes without a large CPQ migration. Monitoring: add metrics for approval latency, %discount by sales motion, and regression alerts for deal close rate post-rollout. Post-launch: schedule retrospective 30 days after rollout and iterate on bands (we may add a 10% band for renewals if friction observed).
